title: private-deployment-acme-weekly-sync-2026-03-23
content:
Weekly sync notes - ACME private deployment (VPC / on-prem)
Date: 2026-03-23
Owner (note author): Liam Chen (SE)
Attendees: Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood PM), Sofia Rivera (CSM), Oliver Brooks (ACME Infra), Noah Kim (ACME Security)
Absentees: --

High-level objective: keep the Private deployment rollout on track for ACME staging -> prod cutover. Confirm VPC peering, KMS/HSM integration, and acceptance test pass schedule.

Agenda:
- Quick status by area (networking, infra, security, app deployment)
- Blockers and escalation needs
- Action items + owners + due dates
- Risks and rollback criteria

Notes / updates:
1) Networking (Oliver / Liam)
- VPC peering: ACME completed routing table changes on their side 2026-03-21. Redwood observed asymmetric route for one AZ; debugged with infra team.
- Current status: peering established, but egress NAT for model telemetry not yet routed through customer firewall.
- Outstanding: Firewall rule (ACME) to allow telemetry IP range 52.48.0.0/16 - ACME to confirm by 2026-03-25.
- Action: Oliver to provide firewall ticket id and expected approval ETA.

2) On-prem infra & k8s (ACME infra / Redwood release-eng)
- Node sizing validated for baseline throughput (3x A100 equiv). Performance tests run 2026-03-20 show 95th percentile token latency within target for small models but degrades under burst.
- Autoscaler tuning needed: current HPA thresholds too conservative. Noah to work with release-eng to adjust CPU/memory thresholds and test again.
- Disk encryption: customer confirmed LUKS at rest; Redwood image needs dm-crypt support (we shipped patch PR #456).

3) Security / KMS (Noah / Maya)
- KMS integration: ACME has HSM in place; key wrap flow verified in staging. Initial failure during key rotate test (2026-03-19) - root cause: service account permissions not set for rotation.
- Action: Noah to add required permissions and rerun rotate test by 2026-03-24.
- Audit logs: Redwood to deliver a sample audit log layout for ACME compliance team (due 2026-03-26).

4) App deployment / Canary (Liam / Maya)
- Canary plan: 2% traffic to private control plane, run smoke tests (latency, correctness), then 10% for 24h.
- Smoke test harness flaky in one test case (streaming chunk reassembly) - root cause may be connection timeout mismatch.
- Temporary mitigation: increase client timeout in canary config; longer-term fix in SDK patch.

5) Acceptance tests / Eval (Maya / ACME QA)
- ACME QA will run perf + accuracy suite. Baseline run scheduled 2026-03-24.
- Criteria for prod cutover: no high-severity failures, 95th latency within SLOs on canary traffic, no KMS rotation failures in 48h window.

Blockers / escalations:
- Firewall rule for telemetry (blocker): prevents telemetry ingestion and alerting; blocking deeper reliability testing. Owner: Oliver Brooks (ACME). Escalation if not done by 2026-03-25 to ACME infra lead + Redwood SRE oncall.
- Autoscaler tuning (medium): prevents realistic burst load testing; Redwood release-eng assigned, deadline 2026-03-26.
- Streaming reassembly flaky test (medium): blocks canary confidence; SDK patch ETA 2026-03-30.

Action items (owner - due)
- Oliver Brooks - provide firewall ticket id and ETA; confirm acceptance of telemetry IPs (52.48.0.0/16) - due 2026-03-25.
- Noah Kim - add KMS rotation permissions and rerun rotation test; report results - due 2026-03-24.
- Maya Patel - deliver sample audit log layout to ACME compliance; include retention semantics - due 2026-03-26.
- Release-eng (assigned: Priya R.) - adjust autoscaler thresholds, run burst test, share results - due 2026-03-26.
- Liam Chen - update canary config to increase client timeout, run smoke tests, document results - due 2026-03-24.
- Eng-sdks (assigned: Marco) - patch for streaming reassembly issue; create PR and test coverage - target 2026-03-30.
- Liam / Maya - confirm QA baseline run schedule and success criteria with ACME QA - due 2026-03-23 (today).

Notes to self / follow-ups:
- Need to capture exact firewall rule text for legal/compliance; ask ACME to attach to JIRA.
- Keep an eye on telemetry volume - if firewall opens but rate-limits, we may see partial ingestion; include throttling test in next run.
- Confirm HSM key rotation window behaviour (what happens if rotation fails mid-request) - escalate to Security PM if unclear.

Risks / rollback criteria:
- If canary shows >2% error-rate increase or KMS rotate fails, immediate rollback to hosted fallback model for ACME tenant. Documented rollback playbook in confluence://acme-private-deploy-runbook.

Decisions made:
- Proceed with canary today after increasing client timeout and rerunning smoke tests.
- Delay full prod cutover until autoscaler burst test passes and firewall rule confirmed.

Next meeting / cadence:
- Weekly sync: 2026-03-30 09:00 PT (same invite) - call owners to update blockers before meeting.
- Interim check-ins: Noah and Oliver to update status in JIRA by end of day 2026-03-24.

Quick TODO for me (Liam):
- Follow up with Priya on autoscaler assignment and ensure runbook steps documented (due 2026-03-24).
- Draft brief for SRE on escalation path if firewall not opened by 03-25.
- Update canary run notes and post results to the shared drive and jira (JIRA-ACME-1245).

End of notes.
